AUDIO TRANSCRIPT
ERA III
Dr. Elias Thorne
Containment Level Four incident. No door failure. No pressure-loss event. No personnel violation. No identified handling error. And yet PT-9 was recovered from an exterior electrical conduit.
The conduit does not connect directly to the culture chamber. Current assumption: contamination entered a polymer cable sheath during maintenance and traveled within the service assembly.
That's not a dramatic breach. Nothing shattered. Nothing broke through a door. The facility remained nominally sealed. Every report asks where containment failed.
I can point at twenty components and say perhaps there. At what point does a facility made of compromised interfaces stop being a containment facility?

AUDIO TRANSCRIPT
ERA V
Laboratory Director
Seal the outer doors. Not to keep it out. To keep people out. Do not enter this facility for samples, equipment, or research archives.
We've lost internal filtration. Level Three has growth inside the service walls. Level Four is inaccessible. Three staff are missing.
We attempted incineration in Isolation Two and contaminated the ventilation trunk. I repeat: do not burn colonies in enclosed circulation systems.
I've transmitted the data to Continuity. If anyone finds this recorder later, the emergency archive is below the main laboratory. Take the data. Leave everything else.
